newsitem.title: PERU: Ashamed Peru police stop requesting bribes.
newsitem.headline: Ashamed Peru police stop requesting bribes.

text.p: Apparently ashamed by their failure to stop Marxist guerrillas seizing the Japanese ambassador's home, corrupt police have stopped extorting bribes from motorists, Lima taxi drivers said on Saturday.
"Their morale is low and they are frightened again like they were a few years ago when terrorism was strong," one taxi driver who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
Peruvian police, who have a bad name for petty corruption, have been on alert since an armed leftist group assaulted the embassy on Tuesday night, taking hundreds of people hostage.
"I have not seen them demanding bribes since this started," the taxi driver said. "It is the only good that has come of this hostage case so far," he added with a smile.
"Let's hope they go on like this. They already had far too much (money)", said another taxi driver, who said he was used to paying police five soles ($2) to get them off his back.
